title: The TCP handshake
hook: Before a single byte of your request is sent, your phone and the server shake hands three times.

steps.caption: Your device reaches out first: "I'd like to start a connection."

nodeCaptions.client: SYN = "synchronize" — this is the opening handshake.

steps.caption: The server agrees, and proposes the same back.

nodeCaptions.server: SYN-ACK acknowledges your request and sends its own synchronize signal.

steps.caption: Your device confirms — now both sides agree the connection is open.

nodeCaptions.server: Only after this third packet does the connection actually exist — real data can flow now.

takeaways: TCP's three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) happens before any real data — it's just agreeing the connection is open.
Both sides need to confirm, not just one — that's why it's three steps, not two.
This overhead is why a new connection feels slightly slower than one that's already open and reused.

quiz.question: What is actually being sent during the TCP handshake?
choices: The full content of your request
Control signals that establish the connection, with no request data yet
quiz.explanation: SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK are all control signals — they set up the connection. Your actual request data only travels after the handshake completes.
